# Appeal of Denial — Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**RE: Molina Healthcare — Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-10**
**Member: Rowan Carter | Member ID: W473677710**
**Reference Number: POC-CD6AF51965-72160**
**Governing Policy: Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404, Shoulder Arthroscopy** ([link](https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf))

Dear Molina Healthcare Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), which was denied on 2026-08-10 with reference number POC-CD6AF51965-72160. I am asking Molina to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in Molina's possession show that the plan's own conservative-care requirements have been met.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I want to walk through what Molina's own policy, MCP-404, requires, and how my records meet it.

The policy states:

> "Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

My records show that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. This has been ongoing for 24 months. On examination, my range of motion was limited by pain and provocative testing was positive on the affected side.

The policy also states:

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My records document more than three months of non-surgical treatment, including:
- NSAIDs for 8 months, with inadequate relief
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief
- Supervised physical therapy from 2026-05-23 to 2026-07-18 (8 weeks, 24 visits completed), documented in the physical therapy discharge note

Taken together, this is more than two forms of non-surgical management, sustained over a period well beyond three months, without lasting relief of my symptoms.

The policy further states:

> "and  Demonstration of functionally limited range of motion (active or passive) on physical examination as compared to the non-involved side"

My exam findings document range of motion limited by pain, consistent with this criterion.

In addition, my MRI dated 2026-07-06 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy — an objective finding that supports the clinical picture described above.

**I also want to note that the specific criteria excerpt provided to me does not include a section titled "rotator cuff repair."** The excerpts I have address diagnostic arthroscopy, debridement, loose body removal, synovectomy, labral repair/biceps tenodesis, distal clavicle excision/decompression, capsulorrhaphy, and capsular release. I am applying the general pain, function, and conservative-care criteria that recur throughout the policy, because those are the criteria the denial itself references. If a different or more specific criteria set governs rotator cuff repair, I am requesting that Molina identify it, as described below.

## Request for the criteria applied to my determination

Molina's own utilization-management materials state that the criteria used are MCG-based and available through the secure provider portal, and that members or their representatives may call to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination. I am formally requesting, in writing, **the MCG guideline title and the specific criteria applied to my determination**, so that I can confirm my records against the exact standard Molina used.

## What I am asking

I am asking Molina to reconsider the denial of CPT 29827, rotator cuff repair, in light of the documentation summarized above, and to provide the specific criteria used in my determination. I am not asking for a guaranteed outcome — only for a full and fair review of the record my surgeon has submitted.

Please let me know if any additional records, forms, or information are needed to complete this review.

**Deadline:** My appeal must be received by 2027-02-06.

**Where to send this appeal:** Molina's appeal process is administered by state. I will submit this appeal through the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com, by calling the Member Services number on my ID card, and/or by mailing it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I understand to be the authoritative address for this purpose.

Thank you for your time and attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Rowan Carter
Member ID: W473677710
Date: [date of signing]
Contact phone: [phone number]
Contact address: [mailing address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
